text: The fact is that the blame for all complaints of that kind is to be charged to character, not to a particular time of life. For old men who are reasonable and neither cross-grained nor churlish find old age tolerable enough: whereas unreason and churlishness cause uneasiness at every time of life.
author: Marcus Tullius Cicero
speaker: Cato
reference: Treatises on Friendship and Old Age
location: Rome or his villa at Tusculum, Italy (presumed)
